A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Auto-Compressing Networks. All 24 pages of v1 and 28 pages of v2, including their appendices, support comparison. Corresponding methods, equations, figures and experiments can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original toy-model, image-classification, language-modeling, pruning, transfer-learning and continual-learning results.

after.justification: v2 retains original vision and language experiments and adds controlled architectural comparisons and early-exit results in Appendices E and H.

M1.justification: The base ACN architecture and Equation 1 remain unchanged. Appendix H adds implemented ACN variants with intermediate classifier branches or a shared early-exit head, weighted intermediate losses and entropy-based exit decisions. These are optional training and inference adaptations.

E1.justification: The synthetic y = 2x regression task in v1 Section 2.3 is removed. CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet-1K, BooksCorpus/English Wikipedia pretraining and SST-2, QQP and QNLI remain. The new architectural and early-exit experiments reuse CIFAR-10 classification.

E2.justification: Appendix E adds evaluated DenseNet-Mixer and DenseFormer-Mixer comparators, while Appendix H adds residual models with branches and shared early-exit heads. The standalone comparison against Aligned, LayerSkip and DeepSup in v1 Section 8.1/Figure 8 disappears. Aligned and LayerSkip remain in the transfer-learning comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces a common 700-epoch comparison and a stated DenseNet depth adjustment for parameter matching. Appendix H adds entropy-threshold testing at 0.7 and FLOP-normalized speedup evaluation. Table 6 adds GFLOPs and storage metrics. These are new evaluation designs; the retained ImageNet, BERT and continual-learning protocols remain substantially unchanged.

E4.justification: The toy compression demonstration and separate intermediate-supervision analysis are removed. New analyses test whether longer training explains architectural advantages and whether ACNs complement early-exit mechanisms. The direct-gradient ablation, task-difficulty study, noise and data-sparsity tests, and BERT pruning analysis remain.

E5.justification: Tables 4 and 6 add uncertainty terms to transfer and ViT/BERT accuracies previously presented without them. The checklist identifies continual-learning spreads as standard deviations. The explicit 1,000-run report disappears with the toy experiment. These reporting changes do not establish that additional runs were performed.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds 700-epoch results, including 92.0 ± 0.08 accuracy for AC-Mixer versus 90.3 ± 0.09 for Res-Mixer. Table 7 adds early-exit speedups up to 3.3×, and Table 6 adds resource measurements. Toy, intermediate-supervision, upstream/per-layer transfer and CPU-latency entries disappear. Noise and continual-learning table values remain unchanged; the additions do not establish cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The general 1D linear propagation equations, assumptions and derivations are retained from v1 Appendix B in v2 Appendix C. The removed toy equations specialize those same expressions, while new Appendix D explains existing residual-summation algebra. Neither introduces or changes a substantive formal result.

C1.justification: The central architectural, 30–80% compression and up-to-18% forgetting claims remain. v2 drops the proposed neurocognitive-model contribution and narrows the stated superiority over intermediate-loss methods from generalization and transfer to transfer. Pruning compatibility remains, with pruning and early-exit synergy framed as preliminary supporting evidence.

C2.justification: The extensive biological/developmental interpretation and the toy study's initialization and imperfect-compression caveats disappear. Appendices E and H add explanations relating slower training to fewer pathways, interpreting the controlled results as better generalization, and linking early-exit gains to concentrated representations. Small-scale evaluation and increased training cost remain acknowledged limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds comparator and early-exit implementation details, explicit transfer settings and a LEONARDO computing acknowledgment. The code-link target changes from anonymous OSF access to a named GitHub repository. The Dirac-style W-hat = I + W disclosure is removed, which does not establish that the underlying implementation changed.

R1.justification: Removing v1's biological-connectivity and developmental-pruning discussion substantially changes the research positioning and removes its associated literature. v2 adds depth-efficiency work by Csordas and Sun, BranchyNet, and foundational BERT/ImageNet citations. Most of v1 Section 10 survives in Appendix A; publication-metadata updates are not substantive changes.

P1.justification: The narrative is extensively condensed and reorganized around compression, generalization, forgetting and transfer. Language modeling moves into the compression section; related work, pruning and the results summary move to appendices. The biological discussion disappears, limitations and broader impact are combined, and a NeurIPS checklist is added.

P2.justification: The document adopts a substantially different conference layout. Task-difficulty panels are merged, transfer and resource plots become tables, and the BERT/pruning figure is split between the main text and appendix. Toy and overview figures disappear, and new comparison tables appear. Figure 1's caption corrects model/dataset attribution while its plots remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The equal-budget CIFAR-10 comparison addresses a training-duration confound in v1, while expanded uncertainty and resource reporting improve empirical assessment. These gains outweigh the loss of toy and per-layer diagnostic evidence, but remain limited: Table 7 omits accuracy alongside early-exit speedups, and Table 5 reports cutoff layer 16 for a DenseNet-Mixer described as having 10 layers. The core contribution receives modestly stronger support.
